forcedChoices.reason: "man of the realm": "reino" collides with "kingdom", and "hombre del mundo" reads as "worldly man".
Same rendering of "realm" as in 129:1.15; plural "realms" is "mundos" (129:4.5).
Spanish has one plain word for "Teacher" and "Master"; John speaks to one person, so "tú".
"your world" as "su mundo" would read as "his world" in a sentence about Jesus.
"may not aspire" can mean permission or ability; "no pueden" keeps both readings.
